subject: Pilot pricing — hybrid seats + throughput experiment
body:
From: Lena Ortiz <lena@patchwork.ai>
To: Hiro Tanaka <hiro_tanaka@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot pricing model question

Hi Hiro,

Quick question as we're lining up our internal procurement for the pilot: do you have a recommended approach for a timeboxed evaluation — seat-based (per-engineer seats) vs throughput (token/credit) billing? Our team expects spiky inference during synthetic tests and lighter steady usage otherwise. Also: if we don't fully consume seats during the two-week pilot, do you offer credit conversion or a short extension instead of a refund? Procurement is already asking about amendment language and PO timing.

Thanks,
Lena
Head of ML, Patchwork Labs

---
From: Hiro Tanaka <hiro_tanaka@redwood.com>
To: Lena Ortiz <lena@patchwork.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 May 2028 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot pricing model question

Hi Lena — great question, and timely. Short answer: we recommend a hybrid trial model for teams with spiky + steady patterns, and we can structure a short experiment so you can evaluate both economics and latency under load.

Proposal (pilot experiment):
- Duration: 2 weeks (standard), with optional 1-week extension at the same pilot rates if milestones or tests need more runway.
- Seats: 3 concurrent developer seats included (used for dev/test/devops access).
- Throughput credits: 200k token-equivalent credits for generative evaluation (usable across endpoints).
- Pricing for the pilot: 20% off our public hosted per-token rate OR equivalent credit value applied to invoice for dedicated trial if you opt for dedicated nodes.
- Conversion path: if you convert to a Dedicated deployment within 30 days, any unused throughput credits roll into the conversion credit (applied to the first invoice); unused seats do not auto-convert but we can offer a one-time credit equal to 50% of unused seat-days toward the conversion invoice.

Attached: high-level pricing worksheet and a short amendment template so your procurement can review language (Patchwork_MVP_spec.pdf, pilot-pricing-proposal.xlsx).

If that sounds like a decent baseline I can loop in Kimberly to confirm invoice cadence and Dev to get an engineering note on what Dedicated would look like for an on-prem / VPC preview.

Cheers,
Hiro Tanaka
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

---
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Lena Ortiz <lena@patchwork.ai>, Hiro Tanaka <hiro_tanaka@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, dev_patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 15 May 2028 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot pricing model question

Lena — adding a few operational details so procurement has clarity:

Billing and legal flow:
- We issue a one-line pilot invoice at the start (covers seats + baseline credits). Final reconciliation invoice issued after pilot showing consumed credits and any overage.
- Payment terms: net 30 (we can accept a PO).
- If you want the optional extension, we add a short amendment (attached: pilot-amendment-draft.docx) — typically sign-off by the AE is enough to activate the extra week.

Measurement & success gates (recommended):
1) Latency SLO validation: 95th percentile under synthetic test < 350ms (hosted) or < configured SLA for dedicated.
2) Cost-per-1000 inference tokens vs baseline: track for conversion judgment.
3) Feature coverage: top 10 prompt flows validated end-to-end.

Small ask from our side: if you need dedicated capacity we typically require a 30-day notice to provision nodes for a short dedicated trial; if you convert midway we can accelerate with a best-effort allocation.

Kimberly Park
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Attachment: pilot-amendment-draft.docx (redlined language for seat/credit conversion, extension clause)

---
From: Lena Ortiz <lena@patchwork.ai>
To: Hiro Tanaka <hiro_tanaka@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@patchwork.ai
Date: Thu, 16 May 2028 11:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot pricing model question

Thanks Hiro and Kimberly — useful framing. A few clarifications from procurement/engineering:

- Could we lower the upfront seat count to 2 for the pilot? We only need 1–2 engineers actively testing, and avoiding unused seat-days helps our CFO.
- We definitely want throughput headroom for the synthetic spiky tests — would you consider trading 25% of the upfront throughput credits for an additional 3 days extension automatically if we exceed X token threshold? That would reduce our risk of needing a manual sign-off for an extra week.
- Dedicated: we may want a short dedicated node run for one heavy test day. Is there a flat daily rate for a single dedicated node we can pre-book during the pilot window?

Procurement is also asking for a DocuSign-ready amendment and an estimated timeline to get a PO out (targeting next Wed). If you can send the amendment with the 2-seat option + the automatic micro-extension clause, I can push that through our procurement queue.

Best,
Lena

---
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Lena Ortiz <lena@patchwork.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Hiro Tanaka <hiro_tanaka@redwood.com>
Cc: dev_patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 18 May 2028 15:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot pricing model question

Lena — thanks for the practical asks. We can accommodate the changes you requested, with guardrails so we keep conversion economics predictable. Summary of agreed tweaks: 

1) Seats: reduce to 2 for the pilot (agreed).
2) Throughput credits vs auto-extension: we can implement an automatic 3-day extension if you consume > 160k of the 200k credits (threshold based). The extension activates automatically and applies at the same pilot rate.
3) Dedicated node day: yes — we offer a dedicated short-run daily rate of $1,200/day for a single node (pre-bookable up to 2 days during the pilot window). This covers allocation and priority support for that day.
4) Conversion credit: when you convert to Dedicated within 30 days, any remaining throughput credits will be converted dollar-for-dollar into a credit on the first invoice; unused seat-days credit remains capped at 50% of unused seat-days as previously discussed.

Kimberly — please prepare a DocuSign-ready amendment (include the auto-extension trigger clause and the 2-seat option) and share the link; procurement target next Wed is reasonable. Dev (cc'd) — can you prepare a short technical note outlining how we handle the dedicated node provisioning and any lead times?

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
VP Sales | Redwood Inference

Attachment references in thread: Patchwork_MVP_spec.pdf (customer spec), pilot-pricing-proposal.xlsx (worksheet), pilot-amendment-draft.docx (redline)
